name: Assumptions vs Unknowns
title: Assumptions vs Unknowns
description: An assumption is something you treat as true without proof; an unknown is something you know you don't know. Both need registry entries - assumptions because they can be wrong, unknowns because they need answers.
how_it_works: Write assumptions as explicit statements with their basis and expiry ('assumed true until test X'), and unknowns as questions needing answers. Review assumptions on schedule - expired assumptions become risks.
key_points: Assumptions: treated-as-true without proof - state and date them.
Unknowns: known gaps phrased as questions needing answers.
Assumptions expire; review them before they rot.
Unstated assumptions are the most dangerous kind.
requirements: A defined build scope with identified unknowns; an owner per uncertainty; a review cadence for registry burn-down.
standards: Risk management practice per ISO 31000; issue/assumption logging per project management standards.
citations: ISO 31000:2018 risk management - guidelines.

name: The Uncertainty Register

Unreviewed registers are decoration.

name: Impact Scoring for Unknowns
title: Impact Scoring for Unknowns
description: Not all unknowns matter equally: impact scoring (what breaks if this stays unknown, and when) prioritizes the burn-down. Score by consequence and by timing - a late answer can be as bad as a wrong one.
how_it_works: Score each unknown on impact (1-5: inconvenience to project-killer) and urgency (when the answer is needed). Work the high-impact, soon-needed unknowns first; park the rest visibly.
key_points: Score impact: inconvenience to project-killer.
Score urgency: when the answer is actually needed.
High impact + soon needed = work first.
Parked unknowns stay visible - parked is not forgotten.

name: Known Unknowns vs Unknown Unknowns
title: Known Unknowns vs Unknown Unknowns
description: Known unknowns are gaps you can name ('we don't know the supplier lead time'); unknown unknowns are surprises. Registries handle the first; contingency and margin handle the second.
how_it_works: List known unknowns in the register, and hold contingency (time, budget, design margin) for the unknown unknowns. After surprises, convert them to known unknowns for next time - organizational learning.
key_points: Known unknowns: nameable gaps - register them.
Unknown unknowns: surprises - cover with contingency and margin.
Convert surprises into registered knowledge afterward.
Margin is the budget for what you couldn't name.

standards: Risk management practice per ISO 31000; issue/assumption logging per project management standards.

Margin proportional to uncertainty - honest, not hopeful.

Replace and re-verify the moment real values arrive.
